title: Commented out `{` and end-of-line comments inhibit Shader Editor Previews
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: 4.7.stable ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon R7 Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 27.20.20913.2000) - AMD A12-9720P RADEON R7, 12 COMPUTE CORES 4C+8G (4 threads) - 7.46 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description When using `FRAGCOORD` (or any other value) in a `.gdshader` after a line that as a commented out curly bracket open, the preview displays a completely different value than before, and seems to default to a `vec4(1.0)` display. _Shows the difference between //{ and only // on the line. Keep in mind that shader previews generally ONLY update AFTER a preview was toggled, and do not automatically refresh when a shader line is changed. The fact that removing the bracket and space from the commented line DID make the previews update is completely unexpected behavior._ I am unsure whether this means the actual data that is returned is different as well. It seems more likely that the parsing for for-loops goes incorrectly, which causes the data to be reset to a default value, since previewing *inside* a for loop is not allowed, or that the assignment isn't properly singled out and turned into a color to display. Ran into this after commenting out a `for (i = 0; i < 10; i++) {` line to use the previews to debug my shader. Both `// {` and `// }` result in the same outcome, and which values is previewed does not seem to matter. Even constants such as `vec4(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` have this issue. The line `// {}` does **not** seem to cause this issue. Might be a similar issue to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/120472. since comments being parsed seems to be an underlying trend in Shader Editor issues. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new Spatial Shader in a ShaderMaterial 2. Apply the ShaderMaterial to a 3D object 3. Select the 3D object 4. Add the following code to the shader ```GDShader void fragment() { vec4 original = FRAGCOORD; // a comment vec4 pre = FRAGCOORD; // { vec4 post = FRAGCOORD; // Incorrect display } ``` 5. Toggle on the previews for all the 3 assignments 6. Any assignment of `FRAGCOORD` after the commented out `{` will display a value of vec4(1.0), while any before do not. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
